name: Mercury
blurb: MESSENGER topography (USGS global DEM) and gravity (JGMESS_160A).

grids.label: Topography
grids.note: MESSENGER global elevation model (USGS, Becker et al. 2016), made from the spacecraft's camera images; height above a 2439.4 km sphere, averaged from 665 m pixels to 0.25°. The lowest floors are about 5 km deep, the highest ground about 4.4 km up.

grids.label: Free-air gravity
grids.note: JGMESS_160A (Konopliv et al. 2020) at 2440 km, degrees 2–55 with a taper above 35. The C20 flattening term is removed. MESSENGER flew low over the north, so the southern hemisphere is much blurrier.

images.label: Visible colour
images.note: Celestia texture (FarGetaNik) from the USGS MESSENGER colour map, gaps filled with the greyscale mosaic. Brightness stretched for display.

sites.name: MESSENGER impact
sites.note: Ended its mission by hitting the surface at 3.9 km/s, making a crater about 16 m wide.

points.label: Impact craters · 451
points.note: 451 named impact craters (IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature), drawn at true size; the largest are the basins Rembrandt (716 km) and Beethoven (630 km). These are named craters only, not a size-complete population, so a density is not computed here. For scale, the size-complete count gives about 10 per 10⁶ km² for D≥20 km, and model surface ages run ~4.0–4.1 Ga for the heavily cratered terrain, ~3.8–3.9 Ga for the Caloris basin and ~3.7–3.8 Ga for the northern volcanic plains (Fassett et al. 2011; Marchi et al. 2013; Head et al. 2011; Ostrach et al. 2015).

sources: Konopliv et al. (2020), JGMESS_160A gravity, Icarus 335 (copy in tudat-resources)
